name: V2Ray Core
summary: A configurable, embeddable proxy core that composes inbound protocol handlers, rule-based routing, DNS/policy features, and tagged outbound handlers; its local core graph is distinct from any external management or subscription service.

features.name: Feature-oriented core instance
features.description: The core instance hosts registered features and lets inbound, outbound, DNS, policy, statistics, and routing components depend on typed interfaces. The core is an embeddable runtime boundary, not a remote control plane.
benefits: Allows protocol components to depend on narrow feature interfaces
Supports assembling different inbound, outbound, routing, and transport components from configuration
costs: Feature registration and lifecycle ordering increase startup and shutdown coupling
A valid component graph still depends on compatible protocol and transport settings

features.name: Inbound/outbound protocol handler boundary
features.description: Inbound workers accept TCP or UDP connections, build session context, and invoke a configured proxy.Inbound. Outbound handlers wrap a configured proxy.Outbound and optionally apply target DNS strategy, proxy chaining, or multiplexing before dispatching traffic.
benefits: Keeps wire-facing protocol handlers separate from transport and routing orchestration
Supports many protocol implementations behind common inbound and outbound interfaces
costs: Session context and stream settings must preserve metadata across protocol boundaries
Multiplexing, proxy chaining, and DNS resolution add alternate dispatch paths

features.name: Rule-based routing to tagged outbounds
features.description: The router evaluates ordered conditions against routing context, optionally resolves domains according to a configured strategy, and returns an outbound tag or balancing result. It selects among configured handlers; it is not itself a transport protocol or centralized control plane.
benefits: Makes policy decisions independent of individual protocol implementations
Supports DNS-aware rules and balancing without moving routing logic into every inbound
costs: Rule order and DNS strategy affect observable traffic behavior
Routing failures leave the session without a selected outbound and require caller handling

mathematical_views.question: How are inbound, routing, DNS, policy, statistics, and outbound components connected inside one V2Ray core instance?
assumptions: Typed feature interfaces are vertices and component requirements are edges
The graph describes local construction and dispatch, not a distributed control plane
Configuration parsing and generated protobuf details are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: How does an accepted connection become a routed outbound flow?
assumptions: An inbound worker creates session metadata and invokes an inbound protocol handler
The router selects a tagged outbound and the outbound handler dispatches through its protocol/transport implementation
The model abstracts byte framing and cryptographic protocol internals

mathematical_views.question: Which routing context fields and DNS observations lead to a selected outbound tag?
assumptions: Rules are evaluated in configured order and a rule can require DNS-assisted IP matching
A selected tag names a locally configured outbound or balancer
The view does not imply policy correctness or reachability of the selected handler
